seen.cipher: Brewer's calendar: 'The beginning of the letter is in cipher, undeciphered.' (Le Grand, Histoire du divorce, iii; the LP text is French from 'a transcript, dated in the margin at the head: Londres, 22 Oct. 1529'). The cipher leaf itself has not been seen; no decipherment is printed beside it.

prior_art.decode: DECODE list.json (10,106 records) searched for Bellay: the only 1529 hit is R9467 = BnF NAF 4206 no. 5 (Friedmann collection), a KEY record for ciphers of Jean du Bellay and Anne de Montmorency, whose note says it 'refers to BnF ms. francais 3077, fol. 114'; no ciphertext record for this letter; R9467 status N/A, not transcribed.
prior_art.tomokiyo: cryptiana henryviii.htm and elizabeth.htm fetched: no Du Bellay 1529 specimen; Tomokiyo/Lasry blog hits only for Marillac to Du Bellay 1550.
prior_art.lasry: Web search (Lasry, Du Bellay, 1529, chiffre) found nothing on Du Bellay's London cipher; no GL.htm entry known.
prior_art.edition: Le Grand 1688 (iii, fragment) and LP IV pt 3 print the clear part; the modern edition (Scheurer, Correspondance du cardinal Jean du Bellay I, 1529-1535, SHF 1969) was not accessible, so whether it deciphers the opening is unchecked; Bourrilly-Vaissiere 1905 covers only 1527-Feb 1529.
prior_art.literature: Searches (Du Bellay Montmorency 22 octobre 1529 chiffre; Wolsey's fall dispatches) found only BHO calendar pages; no study of this cipher found.

vetting.key_check: A key exists: DECODE R9467 (BnF NAF 4206 no. 5, 1529, Du Bellay/Montmorency, pointing to fr. 3077 f. 114). It is an image on DECODE, not a transcription, and was not applied because the cipher opening was not seen; the task is a key lookup in NAF 4206 no. 5 plus the cipher leaf in the Le Grand ms. / BnF.
vetting.duplicates: Ledger grep (Du Bellay, Montmorency, 6019, Le Grand) and DECODE list scan: no catalogue entry, target or DECODE ciphertext for this letter; the sibling Du Bellay letter of 17 Oct 1529 is LP 6011 (not in this batch).
vetting.closed: Key held on DECODE (R9467, BnF NAF 4206 no. 5, cites fr. 3077 f. 114); needs transcription of the key and of the opening cipher passage, which is only a few lines.

prior_art.decode: DECODE R9263 = Caligula C V f. 78, 'Busshop of Galsgo' to 'Qu of Scotte', 1575, 2 pages, status Decrypted, cleartext inline (private); R3824 = TNA SP53/10 James Beaton to Andre Beaton, 1575-77, Decrypted; Tomokiyo's note on R3824 says the key is on the next folio R3825, same as R4000 (SP53/23/34).
prior_art.tomokiyo: DECODE note by Tomokiyo (1 Oct 2023) on R3824 gives the key location; the Lasry-Biermann-Tomokiyo Cryptologia paper (2023) identifies the Mary-Beaton cipher MB (Feb 1576 onward) and the earlier 'chiffre de Raulet'.
prior_art.lasry: Cryptologia 2023, 'Deciphering Mary Stuart's lost letters from 1578-1584' (web search), covers the MB cipher from Feb 1576; the Aug 1575 letter is earlier.
prior_art.edition: Labanoff (1844) prints Mary-Beaton correspondence; no edition of this Aug 1575 letter found.
prior_art.literature: Searches (Beaton cipher 1575 brother; Caligula C III / C V Glasgow) found only the BL catalogue and the MB paper.

vetting.key_check: A key is held on DECODE for the same sender and year: R3825 / R4000 (SP53/23/34) per Tomokiyo's note on R3824, with R9263 a decrypted 1575 Glasgow letter. Not applied: no image of the Planta f. 484 / Caligula C V f. 78 cipher was available.
vetting.duplicates: Ledger grep (Glasgow, Beaton, Caligula C. III, R9263: no hits outside leads) and DECODE scan: R9263 is very likely this same letter (same sender, 1575, to his brother, includes a cipher; Planta's C III f. 484 vs the newer C V f. 78 description) but identity is inferred from catalogue wording, not from the leaf.
vetting.closed: A 1575 Beaton cipher key is on DECODE (R3825/R4000) and the probable same letter is DECODE R9263 (Decrypted); the work is lookup and identity check, not a new break.
